Good morning. The 15th Plenary Meeting of the General Assembly is called to order. The Assembly will begin its consideration of Agenda Item 64, entitled Use of the Veto, to hold a debate pursuant to Resolution 276/262 of April 26th, 2022, on the situation as to which the veto was cast at the 10,000th meeting of the Security Council on September 18th, 2025. The documentation under this item is listed in the Journal of the United Nations. I will now make a statement as the President of the General Assembly.
A simple no.

It might look mundane whenever a permanent member of the Security Council casts a veto. An almost effortless act. Yet the effects are consequential. They reverberate far beyond the Security Council chamber, beyond New York, felt by communities across the world. A veto can extinguish hope for those trapped in conflict. It falls hardest on those who turn to the United Nations for peace, for relief, for a path out of suffering, for hope. And when it results in constant blockages, it can damage the credibility of this whole institution. The Charter makes clear that the Council carries the primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security under Article 24. Yet the veto is not a privilege. It is a responsibility entrusted to 5 nations to be exercised rarely, in the spirit of peace and security for all. That responsibility must never forget the lives it touches. Lives like those in Gaza, where the situation is catastrophic. In the past days, weeks and months, Men, women, and children have been killed by sheltering or waiting for food. Those who survive are mourning the cold tents. They are starving. They are searching for clean water. Thousands of children without parents. At the same time, hostages remain in captivity in unimaginable conditions. Their families wait in torment, not knowing whether they are alive or dead. A situation that is politically and morally unacceptable, and where the world is wondering where the United Nations is. The situation in Gaza is precisely the kind of crisis where the United Nations is called upon to act. Where failure to act undermines the credibility of this organization itself. Therefore, we owe it not only to the people of Gaza, but also to our institution, if we are to preserve faith in it, to act now. Especially as it is clear what must be done. The world calls for an immediate ceasefire. For unhindered access to humanitarian aid, and for the immediate release of all hostages. As a deeply regrettable deadlock of the principal organ of the United Nations tasked with maintaining peace and security erodes global trust in the United Nations itself, it is therefore important that today member states take up this responsibility by bringing this topic to the General Assembly, the heart of the United Nations, through the debate on the use of the veto. The veto initiative, as many of you know, existed since 2022. In that time, 20 vetoes have been cast. And each time, the General Assembly has stepped in to provide an essential measure of accountability. As the United Nations' most representative organ, which is empowered by Article 10 of the Charter to deliberate on matters of peace and security. Each time this Assembly has been convened, it ensured that the veto is not exercised in silence, but subject to the scrutiny of the international community. Excellencies, also today the Assembly underlines by this plenary meeting that it is not the United Nations as an institution failing on Gaza. UN staff is even risking their lives to overcome the blockage of humanitarian aid. And the wider membership of this organization has spoken with clarity. The resolution vetoed in the Security Council contained the core demands that were already adopted by this Assembly: an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire respected by all parties; the immediate and dignified release of all hostages held by Hamas and other groups; and the immediate lifting of all restrictions on the entry and distribution of humanitarian aid throughout Gaza, delivered safely and at scale by the United Nations and its partners in respect to international humanitarian law and its obligations. These same demands were reaffirmed only weeks ago in the New York Declaration endorsed by a large majority of states. And the good news is that since the moment the veto debate has been put on the agenda, these demands, together with last week's high-level international conference on the two-state solution, have already had an impact, including the clear call that annexation will never be accepted. On Monday, the President of the United States presented a plan building on earlier proposals from Arab Muslim countries, European states, the United States itself, and many, many other countries around the world for an immediate and permanent ceasefire. A massive increase in humanitarian aid, and the release of all hostages. These calls now have to be implemented without delay or reservation by both the Israeli government and Hamas. If implemented, it would finally offer the opportunity to end the war in Gaza, as outlined by the many GA resolutions, We must seize this chance to end the suffering in Gaza now. The Israeli-Palestinian conflict cannot be resolved through endless war, permanent occupation, or recurrent terror. The only path to lasting peace, security, and dignity for both Palestinians and Israelis is a two-state solution. After the war, as many countries and the General Assembly underlined at the beginning of this week, We need sustained dialogue, credible negotiation, and tangible steps towards releasing— realizing the two-state solution in line with the UN Charter, international law, relevant UN resolutions, and the New York Declaration. That is the path to justice, that is the path to peace, and that is how we uphold the principles and the credibility of this organization. Thank you.

Not as a substitute to them.

What is the measure of success? It is Palestinian self-determination and the independence of the State of Palestine. That is the single most important contribution to peace. And a legacy-defining achievement. It will change the face of the region and the fate of its peoples. It will lead to the implementation of the two-state solution and to the peace and stability we all need. It will pave the way for regional integration, a prospect many thought and still think impossible, and that is within grasp if we collectively decide to rid this region of wars and occupation and finally choose shared peace, shared security, and shared prosperity. It is time to end this conflict once and for all, so people never experience such pain and loss again, and all peoples can live in peace and security. Peace, a billion times much better than war. Peace saves lives. War takes lives away from us. Madam President, the Palestinian people have a right to life, to liberty, to security, and to dignity. All peoples have a right to live in peace and security. What we need is not a pause in the violence and the injustice, but an end to all of it. Violence is an impasse. It must not be fueled nor tolerated. It must be stopped. And the Palestinian people must be availed protection without delay— protection for their lives, their dignity, their humanity. Likewise, injustice must never be justified or shielded. It must be brought Palestine is committed to peace. We must all seize this opportunity to end the suffering and work for freedom and peace, regardless of how great the challenges are. Thank you, Mr. President. We owe it to those who were killed. We owe it to those who survived. We owe it to future generations. It is time for peace. Thank you very much, Madam President.

Madam President, on Monday, President Trump put forward a roadmap to peace. Prime Minister Netanyahu accepted it. For the first time in many months, there is a clear path forward— a path to bring our hostages home— a framework to end the war. This framework gives hope. Hope that families will be reunited. Hope that the people of Gaza can find a brighter future. Hope that peace in our region is possible. It is an opportunity for nations to choose action over theater. to support practical steps toward peace. Many countries have already pledged their support. Hamas has not yet accepted it. The decision is theirs. But they should know this: it can be done the easy way, or it can be done the hard way, but it will be done.

Thank you.

If they reject the plan, Israel will finish the job and bring every hostage home. This is what action looks like. President Trump and his team worked day and night. They listened. They built a roadmap based on reality on the ground. Meanwhile, here in this Assembly, We have seen great shows of theater, long speeches, grand declarations, staged walkouts. But speeches do not free hostages. Words do not stop terror. Weeks ago, in the Security Council, we saw a draft resolution that failed to condemn Hamas for its massacre on October 7th. Failed to recognize Israel's right to defend itself, and legitimized lies that benefit terrorists. The U.S. vetoed it. We commend their moral clarity in doing so. The fact that we meet here today to recycle failed resolutions that do nothing for peace proves one truth: this body Israel accepted the roadmap because it meets our clear goals to bring the hostages home, to dismantle Hamas, and to guard against renewed aggression. But let me be clear: it is not Israel's plan. It is by no means perfect for us. It has required significant compromise and difficult choices. Believe me, it is not easy to make these concessions. With a heavy heart, we agreed to release 250 convicted terrorists serving life sentences, and 1,700 terrorists detained since the war began. With painful reluctance, we agreed to possible amnesty for Hamas leaders, the men behind October 7th. At great cost, we agreed to a phased withdrawal from Gaza. Despite these dilemmas, Israel has said yes. Many Arab states are welcoming it. Western democracies are supporting it. This is a coalition effort, not a unilateral move. Madam President, Israel has suffered. October 7th scarred our nation. Children murdered. Families destroyed. Communities burned. Yet Israel has chosen compromise for the sake of peace. Demand the release of the hostages.

Demand disarmament. Madam President, Israel fights for its security, but also for its future. Our future is not endless war. Our future is peace. This chamber has become a stage. The script is written in advance. The votes are decided before a word is spoken. While you perform, I will pray. Tonight, Jews around the world will gather for Yom Kippur, the holiest day of our year. Together, we will rise and plead, Avinu Malkeinu, our Father, Our King, release the captives. For us, this is not only a prayer. It is a vow. Master of the universe, the one who saves and delivers, may he redeem in his great mercy our captives from the hand of cruel and harsh enemies. cruelty.

The Palestinian cause is not simply an unresolved political issue. Madam President, I have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of the 10 elected members of the Security Council, namely Algeria, Greece, Guyana, Pakistan, Panama, the Republic of Korea, Sierra Leone, Slovenia, Somalia, and my own country, Denmark. We, the E10, were elected by this very Assembly and entrusted with the solemn responsibility to maintain peace and security. It was in this spirit that we put forward a draft resolution aimed at addressing the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, including the declaration of famine in Gaza City, while also demanding the release of all remaining hostages held by Hamas, suffering in captivity since the horrific attacks on October 7th. Madam President, for nearly 2 years, civilians in Gaza have endured a humanitarian crisis of catastrophic proportions. Vast areas lie in ruins. Homes, schools, hospitals, all reduced to rubble. Civilians have been forced to flee repeatedly, and the majority of population is now displaced with little access to safety or shelter. Hospitals are collapsing under impossible strain. All the while, aid deliveries remain heavily restricted. Food rots on the border while civilians starve on the other side. We are now all painfully aware that famine is present in Gaza. Entire families face daily shortages of food, clean water, medicine, and fuel. Children in particular bear the brunt, suffering from starvation, malnutrition, and disease. Meanwhile, the Israeli military campaign continues to expand in scope and intensity. particularly in Gaza City. The longer the conflict continues unmitigated, the deeper the humanitarian catastrophe will grow and the greater the risk of further regional escalation. As elected members, we believe that the Council should not remain silent in the face of such devastation. When civilians are subject to relentless suffering, it is our duty to respond with resolve. Madam President, the draft resolution had 3 urgent demands, demands that many in this Assembly have made time and time again. First, an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in Gaza respected by all parties. Second, the immediate, dignified, and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other groups. And third, that the government of Israel immediately and unconditionally lifts all restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza and ensures its safe and unhindered distribution to the population in need of such assistance, in line with international humanitarian law. Madam President, 14 members of the Council voted in favor of the draft resolution, with only one member voting against. We deeply regret that it was not adopted and that as a result, the Council was once again prevented from responding to the urgent needs in Gaza, and the suffering in the territory has been prolonged. We are encouraged now by recent indications of progress in the negotiations for a ceasefire. We welcome these efforts and hope that they will lead to a conclusive end to the hostilities in Gaza. In closing, the elected 10 members of the Security Council remain undeterred in our commitment to upholding the mandate of the Council to maintain international peace and security, to representing the will and the expectations of this Assembly. I thank you, Madam President.

I thank the distinguished representative of Denmark on behalf of the 10 elected members of the United Nations Security Council. I give the floor to the distinguished representative of the European Union on behalf of the European Union and its member states.

Madam President, I have the honor to speak on behalf of the European Union and its member states. We thank you, President, for convening this debate following the vote in the Security Council on September 18th, 2025. We also thank the E10 for their efforts in tabling a resolution which received the support of 14 Council members. The European Union welcomes President Trump's commitment to ending the war in Gaza, which offers a way out of this devastating conflict, ensuring an immediate ceasefire and release of all remaining hostages, and guaranteeing the provision of full humanitarian assistance to the Gaza Strip, with a central role for the UN and its agencies— all elements that have long constituted core European Union priorities. We call on Israel to fully comply with its obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law. Suffering of the civilian population must stop. To that end, the EU High Representative maintained diplomatic engagement with Israeli authorities to facilitate the delivery and distribution of aid. However, the quantities distributed to the people in need remain insufficient as compared with the needs of the population. We affirm our readiness to engage with Arab partners as well as the United States on their proposals to chart a way forward on reconstruction, in Gaza and build a lasting Israeli-Palestinian peace with a credible pathway to Palestinian statehood. The EU urges all parties to comply with their obligations under international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law. President, we reiterate the essential role of UN agencies, including UNRWA, which provides crucial services to millions of people in Gaza, the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and across the region, including Lebanon, Syria, and Jordan. The EU also strongly condemns the further escalation in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, following increased settler violence, intimidation, the destruction of homes and property, the expansion of illegal settlements, and also terrorist attacks against Israel. The EU will continue to work on further restrictive measures against extremist settlers and against entities and organizations that support them, as well as against Hamas. Last week, Madam President, at the UN General Assembly High-Level Week, the High-Level International Conference on the Two-State Solution, with thanks to France and Saudi Arabia, reaffirmed the unwavering commitment by world leaders to advancing a two-state solution as the only viable path toward a just and lasting peace. The Global Alliance Ministerial, co-chaired by the EU, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and Norway ministers, also convened during High-Level Week and was an opportunity for the participant— participating ministers to discuss a decisive new phase of collective action building on the New York Declaration. The Global Alliance, as a political and Implementation Platform is one of the mechanisms to translate into action the broad international consensus enshrined in the New York Declaration, endorsed by 142 countries. The European Union will play a key role in taking this forward. We must guarantee that both Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace, security and dignity. The EU is ready to contribute to all efforts towards the two-state solution and calls on all parties to refrain from actions that undermine its viability. We will continue supporting the Palestinian Authority to help it address its most pressing needs, build institutional capacities, and implement its reform agenda. The EU has put together an unprecedented financial package of €1.6 billion for the years 2025-2027 in order to help the Palestinian Authority with the extremely challenging situation and support its reform efforts. We have also launched the Palestine Donor Group. Dear friends, any future Palestinian state must be viable also from an economic point of view, and this can only be achieved with the collective support, including from the Palestinians' neighbors. We urge and invite everyone to join the Palestinian donor group and this effort. Thank you.

We welcome the call echoed in the New York Declaration, which Liechtenstein has endorsed, that Hamas should end its rule in Gaza and disarm. The parties to the conflict should urgently work together towards an agreement on the basis of this plan. It is long past time to end the civilian suffering in Gaza. Madam President, we encourage those behind an agreement to end the war to bring the agreement to the Security Council for formal adoption. The UN was created as a peace organization which, through its Security Council, would be able to end war with binding force on parties. The Security Council, in turn, can mandate decisive action on behalf of every member state. Liechtenstein again urges timely and decisive action by the Security Council Security Council, and if this is not forthcoming, urgent action by this Assembly, especially since many previous agreements were never fully implemented. Madam President, all those committed to ending the war in Gaza must act on the simple maxim: there is no peace without justice. In the Rome Statute on the criminal International Court, states have agreed that those who commit such crimes should as a priority be tried in their domestic legal system. It is only when this is not possible that we must resort to international judicial institutions with the purpose not only of ending the war but to demonstrate beyond doubt that it should never have been waged. Madam President, Liechtenstein mourns for all those needlessly killed in this conflict— mothers, fathers, sons, and daughters— by weapons of war and through starvation. To hold perpetrators accountable is the least we can do in service of their memory. It is time to begin the process of making sense of the senseless, to uphold the promise made to all those who mourn their lost children, as it was to Abraham, for Jews, Muslims, and Christians alike. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Liechtenstein. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Luxembourg.

Madam President, Luxembourg aligns itself with the statement made by the European Union. I will complement it with some remarks in a national capacity. Madam President, we thank you for convening this meeting. following the vote that took place in the Security Council on September 18th. We regret the veto cast by the United States, which once again prevented the adoption of a resolution concerning Gaza, which was proposed by the 10 elected members of the Council. We commend the efforts led by Denmark And the E10, whose draft resolution received the favorable vote of 14 Council members. This draft resolution focused on humanitarian issues was not adopted, even though the population in Gaza is facing extreme distress, famine, repeated forced displacements, and attacks day and night against civilians, hospitals, and journalists. No one can remain indifferent in the face of such a catastrophe. The veto blocks the adoption of a text that included 3 demands which should, in principle, be the subject of international consensus. First, an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire. Secondly, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other groups; and third, Israel's compliance with its international legal obligations and the immediate and unconditional lifting of all restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza. Luxembourg urges all parties to fully respect their obligations under international law and international humanitarian law. as well as the fundamental principles of humanitarian action. Humanitarian aid must never be instrumentalized for political or military purposes, and it must reach the civilians who vitally need it. In this regard, the role of the United Nations and its agency— agencies, particularly UNRWA, is essential in assisting the population of Gaza, the West Bank, and the entire region. Madam President, let us act together with determination to break the cycle of violence. Nothing justifies the continuation of the war in Gaza. More than ever, international solidarity must prevail, and all lives must be protected. Luxembourg is committed to this, and our objective is clear: To enable Israel and Palestine to live side by side in peace and security within safe and recognized borders. That is why Luxembourg recognized the State of Palestine on September 22nd from this very podium during the Conference for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution. The veto of September 18th has not diminish the determination of the international community to redouble its efforts to ensure the viability of the two-state solution and to work towards a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace in the Middle East. And we hope that the plan presented by the President of the United States on September 29th will further strengthen this momentum. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Luxembourg, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Egypt.

Madam President, if Israel possesses an excess of power and arrogance that has led it to intensify its assaults and boast about the killing of tens of thousands of our Palestinian brethren, children, women, and defenseless civilians in Gaza during that wanton war, then Egypt and Arab and Islamic nations also possess an abundance of self-confidence, willpower, and capabilities that reinforce our determination and ability to guarantee the right of the Palestinian people to establish their independent state, a unified state for that proud and noble people on their geographically contiguous territories along the lines of the 4th of June, 1967. From this firm standpoint, Egypt and its brothers from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Jordan, Turkey, Pakistan, and Indonesia have supported the genuine— the genuine initiative and efforts of the U.S. President Donald Trump to end the war in Gaza, to stop the bloodshed, and achieve security for all while restoring the foundations of lost trust in the Middle East. In this vein, we reaffirm our confidence in President Trump's ability to find a path to peace. We express our readiness to cooperate positively and constructively with the United States and all concerned parties to finalize the agreement and ensure its implementation, and to open horizons for peace, achieving security, stability, and peace for all the peoples of the region. In addition to ensuring the delivery of sufficient humanitarian aid to Gaza without restrictions, Preventing the displacement of Palestinians, releasing hostages, establishing a security mechanism that guarantees the safety of all parties, complete the total Israeli withdrawal, the reconstruction of Gaza, and establishing a just peace process based on the two-state solution whereby Gaza is fully unified with the West Bank and a Palestinian state. in accordance with international law as a key to achieving regional stability and security. We also look forward with great hope to the Security Council fulfilling its primary responsibility in maintaining international peace and security, thus contributing to ending the war in Gaza, initiating a settlement process, and achieving peace. Especially that the Council has all the tools and references for a just and comprehensive settlement of the Palestinian question through its resolutions. This, in turn, will enhance confidence in the multilateral system as a whole. From this platform, we reaffirm to our Palestinian brothers again that Egypt will always be your supporter and your ally, as you have known it to be. Egypt will continue to exert all efforts to support you in obtaining all your legitimate rights and to alleviate your suffering. Following the announcement of a ceasefire, Egypt will host an international conference for early recovery and reconstruction in Gaza in cooperation with the United Nations, the Palestinian Authority, and international partners to mobilize support and resources necessary for the rehabilitation projects and for rebuilding the Gaza Strip. This would allow us to heal the wounds, restore normal life in the Gaza Strip, and create conducive conditions for stability. In conclusion, Madam President, Egypt will continue to exert maximum efforts in coordination with the various parties and international actors It reiterates time and again that ending the occupation and reaching a just and comprehensive settlement of the Palestinian question is a historic milestone and an inevitable necessity dictated by considerations of justice, international legitimacy, and the requirements for achieving security and stability at both the regional and international levels. Thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Egypt, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Jordan.

Thank you, Madam President. At the outset, I would like to thank you for convening this important session. We are meeting today while the Security Council is unable to undertake its responsibility in maintaining international peace and security. There is an unprecedented catastrophe caused by the Israeli aggression on the Gaza Strip, which has claimed the lives of more than 66,000 Palestinians since it started 2 years ago. This constitutes a blatant violation of international law, of international humanitarian law, and the decisions of the ICJ. We reaffirm our rejection of the use by Israel of starvation as a weapon of war. This has led to an increase in malnutrition, leading to the death of more than 450 people, including 150 Palestinian children. We reiterate our calls for an immediate and comprehensive cessation of aggressions on the Gaza Strip, and we reaffirm the need to allow the delivery of humanitarian assistance to the Gaza Strip at scale and immediately in order to end this unprecedented suffering. At the same time, the health sector in Gaza has been greatly devastated. Israel has destroyed more than 22 out of 36 hospitals, while hospitals are also lacking 70% of basic medication. Madam President, we seize the occasion to welcome the leading role of the U.S. President and his genuine efforts to end the war in Gaza. We appreciate his proposal to end the war and to rebuild Gaza, to prevent the displacement of the Palestinian people, and to push forward comprehensive peace. We also welcome his declaration that he will not allow Israel to annex the West Bank. We reaffirm our readiness to cooperate constructively and positively with the United States and international partners and regional partners to adopt and implement the agreement. Madam President, Your Excellencies, Jordan condemns the Israeli illegal and unilateral practices in the occupied Palestinian territories, including the ongoing settlements, the confiscation of land, terrorizing the people, and besieging the Palestinian Authority. And people, in addition to illegitimate attempts to undermine the two-state solutions. We reaffirm the importance of the Jordanian custodianship over the Arab and Islamic and Christian identity of the holy sites. We also condemn the Israeli aggressions against these holy sites, the incursion of the settlers into Al-Quds al-Sharif in violation of the legal and historic status of these sites. We remind Israel, as the occupying power, of its obligation, and we reaffirm that Jordan is ready to send hundreds of trucks daily to the Gaza Strip as soon as Israel lifts its illegal measures imposed on the delivery of humanitarian assistance. In the same vein, we reaffirm our support to all the efforts made by Egypt the State of Qatar and the United States in order to reach a deal that would impose a ceasefire in Gaza. We also welcome the International Conference on the Peaceful Settlement and the Implementation of the Two-State Solution in New York on the margin of the 80th session of the GA. That conference has recognized the Palestinian state, and we commend the efforts of the KSA and of France in co-chairing this high-level international conference for the settlement of the Palestinian question and the implementation of the two-state solution. In conclusion, Madam President, we reaffirm that the Palestinian people have the right to their legitimate rights, and this is the basis of comprehensive and lasting peace. This organization, in its— in all its agencies, is the guarantor And we should allow the Palestinian people to establish an independent sovereign state along the lines of the 4th of June, 1967, with East Jerusalem as its capital, based on the two-state solution. This is the only way to achieve a just and lasting peace that would guarantee all the Palestinian rights. Thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Jordan, and I now give I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Austria.

Madam President, We meet in this hall today because one of the permanent members of the Security Council cast a veto on a resolution presented by the 10 elected members of the Council. This is highly regrettable, particularly given the unity that was demonstrated by the other Council members in the face of the horrific humanitarian situation in Gaza. Members of the Security Council, and especially the permanent members, serve on behalf of all of us. They were conferred a special responsibility through the UN Charter. This is why Austria strongly supports the holding of today's debate in conformity with General Assembly Resolution 76/262. On substance, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is nothing short of catastrophic. Too many civilians, too many children have lost their lives. The suffering of the civilian population must stop immediately. For Austria, it is clear the attacks by Hamas on Israel on October 7th were horrible beyond imaginable brutality. They must be condemned by all of us. At the same time, nothing justifies the devastating humanitarian catastrophe we are witnessing in Gaza. Civilians must be protected at all times. There is no justification for violating international law, including international humanitarian law. This war must end immediately. and all hostages must be freed now. And more humanitarian aid must reach the suffering civilians in Gaza without any further delay. We commend the efforts led by the United States and others to achieve a swift end to this war. With the latest US initiative, a concrete plan is now before us. It is now up to Hamas to release the hostages and lay down its arms. Our vision, the Austrian vision, and not just the Austrian vision, is clear: a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in the Middle East. 2 states, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders. Austria's support for the 2-state solution is not just words. Our president, Van der Bellen participated in last week's 2-state solution conference co-sponsored by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and France. And we have supported both as an EU member state and also bilaterally the Palestinian Authority for many decades. I am under no illusion that our shared goal of a 2-state solution faces greater challenges today than ever before. Yet these recent months have only strengthened our conviction that the two-state solution remains the only viable path to peace. Madam President, a sustainable long-term solution must rest on a few core principles. First, international law must guide every stage of this process, from managing current conflict to future negotiations. Second, Gaza is and must remain Palestinian. Palestinian. Any calls for displacement or annexation of Palestinian land are illegal and will only lead to more chaos and violence in the region. Third, Austria rejects any unilateral attempts to undermine the prospects for a two-state solution. The expansion of settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, particularly in the West Bank, is a clear violation of international law and an obstacle peace. We demand that Israel halts all construction of additional settlements. Today is also Yom Kippur. It's a day of forgiving each other. Maybe that's a good moment. And finally, the terror regime of Hamas has no place in Gaza's future. Hamas must not be part of any legitimate governance framework. Israel's security is legitimate. Are non-negotiable and must be fully respected by all sides in this context. In conclusion, let me reiterate that we stand ready to work with our European, Israeli, Arab, and all other international partners to create the conditions for a viable peace process, one that delivers security, dignity, and prosperity for Israelis and Palestinians alike, and one— and the whole region and one that guarantees stability for the region and beyond. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of Austria, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of France.

Madame la Présidente.

Madam President, France reiterates its call for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire and will not stop requiring the immediate, unconditional, and dignified release of all hostages. We reiterate our condemnation of the terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on October 7th, 2023, whose tragic anniversary we will commemorate next week. Hamas can have no place in Palestine's future. Madam President, the resolution presented by the elected members of the Security Council on September 18th had that precise purpose, to respond to the unacceptable humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza and reiterate the urgency of a ceasefire and require the immediate and unconditional release of the hostages. That text did not succeed, which we regret. The situation remains dire and we must act. We welcome the plan proposed on Monday by President Trump to end the war in Gaza, and we call on the parties to the conflict to cease it without delay, to restore a horizon for peace and collective security in the region. France stands ready to contribute to the implementation of this plan in accordance with the principles of the New York Declaration on the two-state solution. Implementing the two-state solution requires the establishment of a sovereign Palestine state— Palestinian state led by a reformed and strengthened Palestinian Authority. That is why France alongside 11 other countries, launched an emergency coalition for the financial sustainability of the Palestinian Authority. The goal is to stabilize its finances and preserve its ability to govern, provide essential services, and maintain security. In Gaza and the West Bank, we reiterate our firm opposition to any plans for annexation, occupation, Or forced displacement of the Palestinian population. We condemn in the strongest terms the Israeli offensive in Gaza City, which lacks military logic and has tragic humanitarian consequences. France reiterates its condemnation of settlement activity. The E1 settlement project in the West Bank seriously undermines the two-state solution. France calls on Israel to respect its international obligations. Respect for international humanitarian law is imperative and non-negotiable. Civilians must be protected. The use of famine as a weapon of war may constitute a war crime. All obstacles to the delivery of aid must be lifted immediately, and such aid must not be instrumentalized for political or military purposes. The plan proposed by President Trump also recalls the central role that UN agencies must play in delivering aid. France will continue to work towards the implementation of the two-state solution endorsed by 142 states. The New York Declaration supports a reformed Palestine Authority, the disarmament of Hamas and its exclusion from Gaza's governance, as well as the stabilization and reconstruction of Gaza. Madam President, last week, 2 hopes were born here: the broad support of this Assembly for the 2-state solution and the development of the peace plan by the President of the United States presented in Washington. France resolutely supports them for the peace and security of Israel, Palestinians, Israelis, Palestine, and the states of the region. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of France, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom.

Thank you, President. The United Kingdom voted in favor of the draft Security Council resolution proposed for adoption on 18th of September, in line with our longstanding demand for urgent action to address the appalling humanitarian situation in Gaza, bring the hostages home, and end the conflict. Since Hamas's atrocities of October 7th, hostages have been held in unimaginable conditions in Gaza. We reiterate our condemnation of Hamas and its terrorist ideology. Hamas must have no role in the future of Gaza. They need to disarm and end their rule. However, the path to peace must be through dialogue and diplomacy, not further bloodshed. The UK condemns Israel's reckless expansion of its military operation, which has already cost the lives of 65,000 Palestinians. We are witnessing an entirely man-made famine in Gaza and are shocked by images of starving Palestinians killed while desperately seeking scraps of food for their families. This is abhorrent. We urge Israel to ensure the protection of civilians and immediately lift its restrictions on the entry of aid to allow the UN and humanitarian agencies to save lives in line with its obligations under international humanitarian law. As my Prime Minister said this week, we welcome U.S. efforts to develop a plan for sustainable peace. We call on all sides to come together and to work with the U.S. administration to finalize this agreement and bring it into reality. Hamas should now agree to the plan and end the misery by laying down their arms and releasing all remaining hostages. Together with our international partners, we will continue to work to achieve consensus on a permanent end to the conflict and a pathway towards a peaceful, peaceful future. President, the UK's historic recognition of the State of Palestine last week is part of our commitment to protecting the viability of a two-state solution, the only path to a just and lasting peace, and to security for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Indonesia.

Madam President, thank you for convening this meeting. Once again, we gather here to respond to the paralysis of the Security Council and the disconnect between the veto power and global conscience. On September 16th, Commission of Inquiry determined that genocide has been committed and continues to be committed against the Palestinians in Gaza. Yet just 2 days after, on its 10,000th meeting, the Council was again unable to adopt a resolution that would have called for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire. fire and lifted all restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza. Hence, over 2 million Palestinians remain under siege and under unprecedented humanitarian catastrophes. The Council's inability to adopt the resolution due to a veto should not be seen as a merely Council procedural failure. but a responsibility once again unfulfilled. Madam President, a permanent ceasefire in Gaza is the indispensable first step towards the unhindered flow of humanitarian assistance and to create conditions conducive for peace talks. All efforts must be taken to achieve this. In this regard, we commend the 10 elected members of the Security Council who have put forward the draft resolution in the pursuit of the ceasefire. We also observed that the majority of nations are advancing efforts to resolving the humanitarian crisis in Palestine and safeguarding the 2-state solution, as has been reflected by the endorsement of New York Declaration a few weeks ago in this hall. Mindful of different perspectives, and approaches towards the peace process, it is important to underline that true peace is not one unilaterally imposed. It requires a genuine and inclusive process guided by internationally agreed parameters. This is in line with the calls made by many leaders last week during the High-Level Week that the 80th year of the UN must serve as a pivotal moment to recommit to the integrity of international law, including on the question of Palestine. Madam President, this Assembly must serve as a platform to show that nations are responsive to global conscience and are therefore steadfast to protect humanity and end the great suffering. Together, we must send a message that any viable political solution to the Palestinian question must address the fundamental issues of colonialism and historical injustice. Our focus must extend beyond today. The repeated misuse of veto power has eroded trust in the multilateral system. Therefore, the Security Council must be reformed to ensure that accountability prevails and the veto power does not allow atrocities atrocities go unchecked. Indonesia reaffirms its unwavering commitment to stand with humanity, and we will continue to work for the United Nations that stands with humanity. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Indonesia, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Malta.

Madam President, Excellencies. Malta aligns with the statement delivered by the European Union, but I would like to make the following remarks in my national capacity. My country, Malta, fully supports supports the content of the Security Council resolution tabled by the 10 elected members, calling for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, along with the release of all hostages and the lifting of all restrictions by Israel regarding the entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza. We thank Denmark in particular for its approach as PEN and the other elected members for their efforts to generate consensus on this resolution. Malta has repeatedly and unequivocally condemned Hamas's terror attacks of October 7th, and we reiterate that the immediate release of all remaining hostages must continue to be a priority. However, the scale of famine and human suffering unfolding in Gaza represents a profound violation of the fundamental principles of international humanitarian law and is, quite simply, indefensible. In the face of such grave suffering, it is imperative that the Security Council calls for a permanent cessation of hostilities. Regrettably, almost 2 full years into this conflict, it has been unable to do so. This has real-world consequences. Every day we have, and we continue to witness, horrific scenes of human tragedy, including increased rates of famine, children severely injured through bombardment, and people who are killed or wounded while seeking life-saving aid. As many leaders, including Malta's Prime Minister, outlined during the general debate in this Chamber only last week, the ending of the violence and bloodshed in Gaza must continue to be a first-order priority for the United Nations. The ongoing war has already cost the lives of more than 65,000 Palestinians, and it has the potential to do even more lasting damage to entire generations of Palestinian children. Malta welcomes all genuine efforts aimed at ending hostilities in Gaza, including the recent proposal announced by the United States. Malta reaffirms its commitment to contributing to concrete initiatives that end this conflict and create a meaningful pathway to peace, which must include a secure Israel existing alongside an independent Palestinian state.

I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Malta, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Qatar.

Thank you, Madam President. I thank you for convening this important meeting. Under the item use of the veto, Qatar expresses its thanks to the elected 10 members of the Security Council for tabling the draft resolution on the situation in Gaza. Madam President, we hold this meeting today after the use of the veto in the Council on the 18th of September with regards to a draft resolution tabled by the elected members on the situation in Gaza. In this context, Qatar expresses its regret that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution that aimed to end the catastrophic suffering of the civilians in Gaza as a result of the continued Israeli aggression, and that called for an unconditional and immediate ceasefire by all parties and the immediate release of all hostages, in addition to calling on Israel to lift all restrictions on humanitarian aid. And guaranteeing the distribution in a safe and unhindered manner through cooperation with the United Nations and other humanitarian organizations. Madam President, the State of Qatar continued as part of its efforts to de-escalate this situation in the region and to preserve the two-state solution for 2 years to reach a settlement that ends the war in Gaza. And we are proud in It is in this context that our mediation efforts together with Egypt and the United States have succeeded in releasing a large number of Israeli hostages and Palestinian detainees, in addition to allowing humanitarian access into Gaza despite the challenges and the complex situation. The State of Qatar has reaffirmed its readiness to continue its active participation and efforts in order to end the war in Gaza within the context of the U.S. President's initiative. This is a continuation of Qatar's approach and commitment to the peaceful settlement of conflicts and in accordance with our role in support of regional peace and security. In this context, we reiterate that we welcome the leading role of the U.S. President Donald Trump and his genuine efforts efforts to end the war in Gaza. And we have supported the plan through a declaration by Arab and Muslim countries, and a declaration issued recently, and that we will continue our efforts with the U.S. to implement peace in the region. And the states have expressed their readiness to cooperate with the U.S. and relevant actors to implement the plan and guarantee its success in a manner that guarantees peace, security, and stability for the people of the region, and out of joint commitment to efforts with the U.S. to end the war in Gaza through a comprehensive agreement that guarantees humanitarian access without restriction and the non-displacement of Palestinians and the release of hostages, and creating a security mechanism that guarantees security for all parties and that guarantees the full withdrawal of Israel and the reconstruction of Gaza and implementing the two-state solution. by which Gaza would be united with the West Bank under a Palestinian state as per international law, as this is the key to achieve regional stability and peace and security. Madam President, Qatar reiterates its welcome of the New York Declaration on the 2-state solution and the establishment of a Palestinian state, which was issued by the High-Level International Conference for the Peaceful Settlement of the question of Palestine. And here we thank the sisterly Saudi Arabia and France for their efforts. And we welcome the successive recognitions of the State of Palestine as a step towards the two-state pollution— solution and a full and just lasting peace. And with the context of our support for the Palestinian people and their just cause, and their right to self-determination as per international resolutions and the Arab Peace Initiative, which guarantees the establishment of an independent Palestinian state on the borders of 1967 with East Jerusalem as its capital. Thank you, Madam President.

I thank the distinguished representative of Saudi Arabia. And I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Portugal.

Gaza and developments in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. Conflict and seeks to promote and protect a just and lasting peace in the Middle East based on the two-state solution. I thank the distinguished representative of Portugal, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of South Africa.

Madam President, thank you for convening this debate for the umpteenth time to discuss the failure of the UN Security Council, entrusted with the maintenance of international peace and security, to once again demand an immediate ceasefire, release of hostages, and full humanitarian access to prevent further wanton death and destruction in Gaza. We are here today because a permanent member used its veto to prevent a halt to a genocidal bombardment and occupation of this narrow strip of Palestinian land yet again. It is tragically symbolic that the Security Council's 10,000th meeting will be marked and remembered for the failure of the Council to come to the aid of innocent people whose lives are being decimated and existence snuffed out through the most heinous means possible: genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. The inadequacies of the UN Security Council, with a decision-making structure that empowers a single permanent member to go against the moral will of almost all other member states of the United Nations should be addressed through urgent Security Council reform to restore the credibility of the United Nations. Madam President, it is deeply concerning that the Security Council has become paralyzed and unable to deliver on its mandate by passing a resolution that would have delivered on the expectations of both the Palestinian and Israeli people for an end to the suffering on both sides. The inability of the Council to take even the most minimal action means that civilians will continue to be exposed to indescribable horrors and atrocities, therefore failing in responsibility to protect civilians in armed conflict. It further renders the Council incapable of of preventing the conflict from spilling over into the wider regional— into a wider regional crisis. We believe that the international community has an obligation to put an end to the ongoing genocide before it is too late. The Gaza Strip has been facing a war of genocide, destruction, starvation, and displacement waged by the Israeli occupation for forces, in which they have injured more than 220,000 Palestinians and killed more than 65,000, the majority of whom are unarmed children, women, and the elderly. Madam President, Israel is perpetrating these violations and crimes willfully and wantonly, confidently knowing that they are allowed through the Security Council veto to act with impunity and are allowed to force its terms for an end to the conflict on the people of Palestine in utter disregard for Palestinian self-determination. All the while, Palestinians continue to face extermination. Israel is violating every provision of international humanitarian law and international human rights law intended to protect civilians. Israel is waging war on the Palestinian people themselves with the brutal use of starvation, displacement, and impoverishment, denial of basic healthcare, denial of lifesaving humanitarian access, and an unjustified campaign against UNRWA and the UN as a whole. Madam President, the so-called E1 plan recently approved by the Israeli government should be rejected. This plan would divide the West Bank into 2 parts and would isolate occupied Jerusalem from its surroundings and would undermine the option of the 2-state solution in a blatant violation of international law and relevant Security Council resolutions. The Israeli government has brazenly denied the possibility of a Palestinian state, while 157 countries recognize the Palestinian state and global community has come together to reaffirm the fundamental importance of a two-state solution. South Africa supported the outcome of the International Conference on the Two-State Solution held in July and the subsequent GA resolution whereby it was adopted. The outcome was a way to give greater impetus to the two-state solution's implementation, trusting that the practical measures and requirements outlined in the outcome could be useful in an inclusive, negotiated, and peaceful resolution on the question of Palestine. Madam President, we reiterate that the international community cannot proclaim the importance of international law and the UN Charter in some situations and not in others, as the rule of law only applies— as if the rule of law only applies to a select few. For international law to be credible, it should be uniformly applied and not selectively. Furthermore, the United Nations Security Council should not be an obstacle to international law and fundamental principles for international law such as jus cogens norms that protect all humanity. The failure or inability of the Security Council to act and respond effectively to conflict situations such as in Gaza has highlighted repeatedly the urgent need for the reform of the Security Council. We cannot afford to delay this any longer. The veto should never block urgently needed action to maintain peace and security. This equally applies to the actual use of the veto as well as it does to the threat of The efforts and initiatives towards limiting the use of the veto have a key role to play in this regard, but can never replace the urgent need for structural reform of the United Nations Security Council. Madam President, South Africa believes that addressing the root cause of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is long overdue. At the center of the root cause is the illegal occupation of Palestine, of the Palestinian territories. Illegal settlements leading to dispossession and displacements and human rights abuses are a flagrant violation of United Nations General Assembly and Security Council resolutions and contravenes international law. The continued policies of the occupying power can only spur hatred and resentment. In conclusion, to promote peace and stability, there is an urgent need for a negotiated settlement towards a two-state solution, which this Assembly and the Security Council has recognized in its resolutions and the acceptance of Palestine as a full member of the United Nations. The situation in Gaza should serve as a catalyst for finding a just and lasting peace for Palestinians as well as Israelis. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of South Africa, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Japan.

Thank you, Madam President. Hamas must immediately release all the remaining hostages. Yet these 2 years have also been a time of unspeakable tragedy for the Palestinians in Gaza. Tens of thousands of innocent people have been killed, wounded, displaced, and left to endure an ever-deepening humanitarian catastrophe, even famine. Israel has intensified its ground operations in Gaza City, claiming yet more lives and exacerbating an already catastrophic situation. As both our Prime Minister and Foreign Minister clearly stated in this very hall, last week. Japan strongly condemns these actions. We call on Israel to immediately cease its military operation and all unilateral measures. It is regrettable the Security Council has thus far failed to act decisively to achieve these goals. A veto must not become business as usual. Reform of the Security Council is crucial for the Council to regain the trust of the member states and the international community. Madam President, on September 29th, President Trump announced a comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict. Japan highly welcomes his leadership and efforts to achieve peace. This is a significant step toward a two-state solution, including a ceasefire, improving the humanitarian situation, and releasing hostages. In this regard, my country has most recently contributed over $3 million to WFP and $6 million to WHO, respectively, for urgent food and medical assistance, adding to the more than $230 million in humanitarian aid we have provided over the past 2 years. Madam President, peace in the region is not born out of war or nourished by hatred. It can only be achieved through a just and lasting 2-state solution where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace. peace, security, and mutual dignity. Together with partners, Japan will continue to pursue diplomatic efforts to make this vision a reality. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Japan, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Mexico.

Madam President. The humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is unconscionable. Every time we meet in this hall, the numbers of the dead, wounded, displaced persons, and victims of famine have swelled at an alarming pace. The dehumanization that these figures allow is equally concerning. The international community cannot stand idly by twiddling its fingers when we are witnessing the clear reduction of the space within which humanitarian organizations are allowed to operate, when we witness the ever-hastening expansion of evacuation orders, shellings and demolitions which are increasingly close to humanitarian facilities, and when we are witnessing the constant use of ammunition in humanitarian aid distribution centers. We need urgent collective actions. To halt and reverse this humanitarian crisis, which has no precedent in recent decades. In view of this heart-wrenching state of affairs, Mexico values the efforts undertaken by the 10 elected members of the Security Council. The E10, through these efforts, proposed a Security Council resolution focused on providing urgent relief to the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Following the veto cast against this draft resolution, my country is compelled to emphasize once again that there can be no justification whatsoever for the paralysis of the Security Council when the life of tens of thousands of people are at stake, and when those lives depend on the very decisions that the Security Council takes. The international community has repudiated the fact that one or two countries in opposition to the majority of the membership are able to veto UN action. Which could result in less death or less hunger for vast numbers of human beings. Allow me once again to reiterate the historic position of Mexico as regards the veto. Since the negotiations on the UN Charter in San Francisco, my country has maintained that the veto does not serve the collective interests of the international community. Rather, it has simply furthered individual political interests of whoever has cast it since then. I wish to take this opportunity to invite all countries that have not yet done so to accede to the Franco-Mexican Initiative on the Suspension of the use of the veto in cases of mass atrocities. It is of pivotal importance to suspend the use of the veto until we achieve its abolition. Given that the Security Council is currently unable to act, Mexico here reaffirms its convictions. Regarding the role that it is incumbent upon this General Assembly to play. They must shoulder their own responsibilities in terms of safeguarding the 3 fundamental pillars of our Charter. The General Assembly recently adopted a resolution on the revitalization of this organ. That resolution contained clear guidelines to facilitate the adoption of measures following a debate on the use of the veto. Let us not allow this opportunity to slip through our fingers, the opportunity to ensure that our action does not simply boil down to empty words issued from this rostrum. Madam President, the New York Declaration adopted by the General Assembly less than a month ago marked a turning point in terms of how member states view the two-state solution. The two-state solution for the consolidation of a Palestinian state state living side by side the State of Israel. However, the ratcheting up of hostilities means that the Palestinian civilian population in Gaza has no viable horizon for what we have come to call the day after war. or for the reconstruction of its social fabric. We must also guarantee that we never again see atrocious attacks such as those that occurred on the fated day of the 7th of October, 2023. Lastly, we wish to echo The words of our Secretary-General. We hope that the peace plans that have emerged in the last few hours will allow an urgent ceasefire, and we hope that they will result in progress towards peace in the Middle East. Thank you.

President, we meet once again to discuss the use of the veto preventing the Security Council from adopting a resolution demanding an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in Gaza. And the unrestricted entry of humanitarian assistance to Gaza. We remain shocked by harrowing images of famine in Gaza and by Israeli military actions that can only be described as grossly disproportionate. Palestinian civilians continue to bear the brunt of Israel's actions. Humanitarian and medical workers continue to be killed, and health facilities and vital infrastructure in Gaza have been almost completely destroyed. For some time, the humanitarian situation in Gaza has been an utter catastrophe. Palestinian citizens have now endured 2 appalling and hellish years since the crisis escalated. We were therefore disappointed that the use of the veto once again blocked a renewed effort to achieve a ceasefire and humanitarian access. The need for the Council to act could not be clearer. President, New Zealand is a longstanding opponent of the use of the veto. We have actively supported the veto initiative since its inception 3 years ago and remain strong proponent of Resolution 76262. The Security Council's legitimacy is fundamentally defined by its ability to exercise its responsibility under the UN Charter to maintain international peace and security. The use of the veto deprives the Security Council of the ability and increases the importance of an empowered General Assembly. Each and every veto impacts the perception of Council's legitimacy and, by extension, the United Nations' broader legitimacy and effectiveness. Despite the Council's failure to adopt this particular resolution, New Zealand's strongly believes the international community must retain its focus on the very urgent and practical challenge of getting as much humanitarian assistance as possible into Gaza. We note that the vetoed resolution which led to this meeting also reiterated a demand for the immediate, dignified, and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas and other groups. This is another point which New Zealand continues to strongly support. Further, we have repeatedly called for a ceasefire and for Israel to allow vital assistance to flow into Gaza. We strongly reiterate these calls once again. Aid must flow. Violence must cease.
